subject: E4.1 v1-dependency F2: eval-mode trailing my/our declaration (value-losing let) — 10 events
description:
DONE s342f (7dba3af). The task's "check each row first" was the right call: the CPAN half was never syntax probes — all four board events are `eval "our $VERSION = '1.01'"`, a routine module idiom.

FIXED:
- `our NAMES OP= RHS` as an eval tail — the gate refused EVERY `our`, though _lower_our_decl already returns the assignment expression as its only form and _lower_block returns () for the empty remainder, so the value was already the tail. Scalar / ||= / list / array all match perl now.
- no-init `our` — v1 answered with the emitted variable NAME (a silent-wrong); now appends the READ, which is what perl gives (`our $A`->5, `our ($C,$D)`->2, `our @E`->2, `our %H`->1, probed).
- `my ()` — legal Perl declaring nothing (perl #113554); my.t asserts `eval "my ()"` leaves $@ EMPTY. Gated in BOTH positions. Tail value is `(progn)` (what a bare `()` lowers to): (p-undef) is a 1-element list and (vector) an ARRAY ref — both measured wrong against perl.
- bare multi `my ($c,$d)` tail = the LIST of its names, lowered through the expression machinery with 'inherit' so both context rules come free.

NO WORK NEEDED (checked per row):
- `my $$x` / `my @$x` / `my %$x` / `my $$$x` (eval.t): the test is `isnt($@, '')` — it only requires a NON-EMPTY error, and v2's TODO satisfies it. These are invalid Perl (principle 9).

RESIDUAL: `my($a,$b),$x,my($c,$d)` (RT #126844, my.t) — a declaration buried in a comma expression, the #138 family. Its assertion is an unconditional pass(), and BOTH pipelines get the value wrong today (perl 5 elements, v1 0), so the flip costs nothing. Recorded in docs/v1-live-share-audit.md F2.

Side effect: sort.t's `eval { our @copy = sort {…} }` block was a v1 seam and now lowers natively (verified 203/1 before and after — that 1 is its blessed baseline row).
